## Definition and Core Concept

RLVR is a rapidly emerging paradigm that aligns both LLMs and other agents through objective, externally verifiable signals. More specifically, RLVR means reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards: training models with reward signals from checkable task outcomes, executable feedback, formal validation, and other verifier-backed signals.

## How RLVR Works

RLVR trains a model to earn a reward only when its output passes programmatic checks. Instead of asking humans which answer they prefer, the system samples multiple candidates, runs them through verifiers, and updates the policy toward behaviors that pass. RLVR couples reinforcement learning with objective, externally verifiable signals, yielding a training paradigm that is simultaneously powerful and trustworthy, with unit tests, formal proofs, or fact-checkers providing binary, tamper-proof feedback.

## Information Extraction Applications

RLVR-aligned models generate schema-valid JSON, forms, and API payloads that integrate cleanly into automated pipelines with minimal manual correction. Additionally, instead of checking a single final answer, you can extract an ordered sequence of verifiable signals from high-quality reference outputs, making it possible to apply RLVR-style training to tasks like report writing, email drafting, customer support responses, and policy compliance.

## Recent Research (2026)

LongRLVR is an ICLR 2026 paper addressing long-context reinforcement learning with verifiable context rewards. Knowledge-to-Verification (K2V) is a framework that extends RLVR to knowledge-intensive domains and enables verification of the model's reasoning process, without any human supervision.

## Key Advantages

This approach eliminates reward model training and provides deterministic feedback, with fast iteration because verifier logic changes don't require retraining.

## Overview

KnowCoder is a Large Language Model (LLM) to conduct Universal Information Extraction (UIE) via code generation. The paper was published in Proceedings of the 62nd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers), pages 8758–8779, Bangkok, Thailand.

## Key Innovation: Code-Style Schema Representation

KnowCoder introduces a code-style schema representation method to uniformly transform different schemas into Python classes, with which complex schema information, such as constraints among tasks in UIE, can be modeled in an LLM-friendly manner. The code-style schema representation method comprises three basic classes, namely, "Entity", "Relation", and "Event". Based on the three basic classes, they represent all the concepts in the schemas by the corresponding classes.

## Schema Library and Scale

A code-style schema library covering over 30,000 types of knowledge was constructed, which is the largest one for UIE. The constructed schema library encompasses over 29,177 entity types, 876 relation types, and 519 event types.

## Learning Framework and Results

KnowCoder contains a two-phase learning framework that enhances the schema understanding ability via code pretraining and the schema following ability via instruction tuning. After code pretraining on around 1.5B automatically constructed data, KnowCoder achieves relative improvements by 49.8% F1 compared to LLaMA2 under the few-shot setting. After instruction tuning, it achieves up to 12.5% and 21.9% improvements compared to sota baselines under the zero-shot setting and the low resource setting, respectively.

## ProUIE: Stepwise Fine-Grained Rewards with GRPO

ProUIE is a Macro-to-Micro progressive learning approach that improves universal information extraction (UIE) without introducing any external information, consisting of three stages: macro-level Complete Modeling (CM), meso-level Streamlined Alignment (SA), and micro-level Deep Exploration (DE).

### Stepwise Fine-Grained Reward (SFR) Mechanism

The Deep Exploration stage applies GRPO together with UIE-specific reward design called Stepwise Fine-grained Reward (SFR), which provides coarse-to-fine supervision over structural units to guide exploration.

The key idea of SFR is to decompose structural correctness into progressively finer units and assign rewards across levels: for NER, SFR defines stepwise rewards at the entity-type and entity-value levels; for RE, at the relation-type, relation-instance, and entity-pair levels; and for EE, at the event-type, trigger, role, and argument levels.

### Benchmark Results

Extensive experiments on 36 public datasets demonstrate that ProUIE consistently outperforms strong baselines, and further delivers clear gains in large-scale production-oriented information extraction.

The approach integrates GRPO (Group Relative Policy Optimization) with this task-specific reward mechanism to improve performance on information extraction tasks including Named Entity Recognition (NER), Relation Extraction (RE), and Event Extraction (EE).
